prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (1997)

Education and skills
- Add £2bn/year for education funded by a 1p rise in the basic income tax rate.
- Universal high‑quality early years places for 3–4 year‑olds; double school books/equipment in year one; cut primary class sizes to max 30 within five years; £500m over five years for repairs; fully fund SEN Code.
- General Teaching Council; stronger inspections; focused Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; literacy drive.
- More school autonomy within streamlined local oversight; phase out Assisted Places Scheme; partnerships with independent schools.
- Individual Learning Accounts; replace student loans with income‑linked repayments; oppose top‑up tuition fees; credit‑based system across post‑14; link all schools to the internet.
- Workplace training: 2% remissible payroll levy (small firms exempt); 16–19s to receive at least two days/week of education or training; new Quality Council.

Economy, tax, jobs, enterprise
- Central bank independence to target low inflation; support joining a single European currency subject to Maastricht criteria, UK compliance, and a referendum.
- Fiscal “golden rule”; separate capital/current budgets; promote public‑private partnerships.
- Convert benefits to “working benefits” for long‑term unemployed; shift tax from jobs/goods to pollution over time; encourage saving and portable pensions.
- Small business finance reforms; statutory interest on late payments; reduce red tape; long‑term abolition of the Uniform Business Rate; regional development agencies; shift R&D from military to civil; stronger competition law; single utilities regulator; tighter financial services oversight.

Environment, transport, energy
- Legally backed targets including a 30% CO2 cut from 1990 levels within 15 years; tax shift to pollution (including phased carbon tax).
- Urban road pricing to fund public transport; London Underground to remain public while accessing private finance; rail targets to double passengers and treble freight by 2010, with sanctions and potential reacquisition of Railtrack control on persistent failure.
- Cut annual car tax to £10 for ≤1600cc, offset by ~4p/litre fuel duty rise; planning to reduce travel demand.
- National home insulation programme for 2m low‑income households; efficiency standards; lower VAT on conservation; support renewables; no subsidies for nuclear and no new nuclear replacements; improved water regulation; stronger wildlife and countryside protections; product design for reuse/recycling; animal welfare measures and bans on specified testing and devices.

Homes, communities, policing
- Build more affordable homes via partnerships; release council capital receipts; new Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers (existing MIRAS protected); merge housing support over time; end street homelessness by 2000; bring empty homes into use.
- 3,000 additional police officers; restorative justice and targeted youth interventions; Crown Prosecution Service overhaul; local crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support; more accountable police governance.

Health and care
- Extra £540m/year for the NHS (funded by closing NIC loopholes and 5p on cigarettes); six‑month halt on finance‑driven closures pending audit; £200m/year for front‑line staff (e.g., 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors equivalent); maximum six‑month waits within three years; end two‑tier GP funding; National Inspectorate for Health & Social Care; national NHS pay framework; restore free eye/dental checks; freeze prescription charges; secure NHS dentistry access; stronger patient rights; greater local accountability; expanded carer support and national care standards.

Constitution and governance
- Bill of Rights incorporating the ECHR; Human Rights Commission; Freedom of Information Act; reform quangos; referendums for constitutional change.
- Commons reform (including reducing MPs by about one‑third), predominantly elected second chamber over two parliaments, proportional representation for all elections, fixed four‑year terms, transparent party funding.
- Devolution for Scotland and Wales with tax‑varying powers; English regional assemblies where demanded; stronger local government; long‑term shift to local income tax and locally set business rates.
- Northern Ireland: power‑sharing executive under PR, rights protections, policing and justice reforms, cross‑border economic bodies.

Welfare, equality, families
- Benefit Transfer Programme for long‑term unemployed; raise personal allowance by £200 (taking ~500,000 out of income tax), funded by a new 50% rate over £100,000; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a Low Income Benefit; national childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; tackle fraud and tax evasion.
- Pensions: earnings‑linked top‑up for low‑income pensioners; flexible retirement 60–70; move toward citizenship‑based entitlements; replace SERPS with universal personal/occupational schemes with portability.
- Restore benefits for 16–17s; statutory youth services; family courts to replace the Child Support Agency; parental leave and flexible parental benefit; support flexible work.
- Strengthened rights and anti‑discrimination measures for women, disabled people, ethnic minorities, and LGBT people.

Foreign policy, defence, development, trade
- Pro‑reform EU stance with greater democratic accountability; conditional participation in single currency; stronger CFSP with national control over deployments; CAP and fisheries reform.
- Maintain defence capability; retain Trident with reduced warheads pending multilateral disarmament; support NATO enlargement and CTBT.
- UN reform: stronger peacekeeping capacity, International Criminal Court.
- Environmental leadership internationally; increase aid toward 0.7% GNP within 10 years; debt relief; human rights conditionality on aid.
- Restrict arms sales to abusive regimes; support UN arms register; ban landmines; advance fair trade, labour standards (via ILO), environmental clauses in trade, and global competition policy.

Tax transparency
- Annual “Tax Contract” to explain revenues/spending, attach costs to pledges, pursue waste reduction before tax rises, and focus on fairness; 70% of adults pay lower or unchanged income tax overall under proposals.
